reference: bench-src/ref/gen_plbbackflow.py — consistency with the published method _plb/bf/METHOD.md (Python, matrix re-typed from METHOD, so the sweeps alone cannot catch a wrong cell) + 14 external anchors worked by hand from the Resideo EN 1717 brochure ch. 7 (pp. 37-44) + second-source cross-check of the matrix X cells per category and the library categories against the SYR guide (17/17)

second_source.source: SYR guide "Drinking water protection in installations" (Hans Sasserath GmbH & Co. KG), pp. 3-10
second_source.scope: device per category and practical examples per category vs the matrix X cells and the library categories; o cells, H/L families and height rules are not covered by this source

reference_citations: EN 1717:2000 Protection against pollution of potable water in water installations and general requirements of devices to prevent pollution by backflow (§4 fluid categories, protection matrix)
Honeywell / Resideo EN 1717 brochure: matrix pp. 45–46, installation dimensions p. 34, application examples ch. 7 (external anchors)
SYR (Hans Sasserath GmbH & Co. KG) guide "Drinking water protection in installations", pp. 3–10 (second source: device per category, practical examples)
Belgaqua TVBI/PTI (EN 806-5:2012 Annex A Table A.1 maintenance intervals are not part of this bench; they are covered by the engine test)
WaterRegsUK / WRAS Backflow protection ratings (Jan 2024), FAQs Type AF / Type AG: AF fluid category ≤ 4, AG ≤ 3 (CR-60)
tolerance: exact on category, admissible set, every exclusion reason, preferred unit, booster, integrated and air-gap-insufficient flags, points per category (sum of n) and their total, number per point (X2-6), counted units and the highest category; air gap to 1e-9 mm; the headline tiles must show the number of points and the highest category

cases.note: height rules DB/DC 150, HA 200, HB/HD 250 mm (strictly greater)
air gap max(3 d, 20 mm) and booster
question chain: first yes decides, unknown = yes, unanswered = no category
hose outlets: HA/HB/HD vs back-pressure and height
custom point: unanswered back-pressure / needs pressure = yes (D-PLB-17); invalid inputs -> point errors (D-PLB-14)
X2-6: n must be a whole number 1..10 000 (missing -> 1); 0, negative, fractional, > 10 000, text, true -> error n, point not counted
X2-6: a category-5 point with n = 0 is not counted - the highest category stays 2 and only the 3 valid units are counted
Y4-4: 24 garden taps -> category 3 = 24 (not 1); WC x10 -> category 5 = 10; heater x2 -> category 2 = 2; n = 0 and an unanswered custom point are not counted
Y4-5: an air gap known to be below max(3 d, 20 mm) is excluded (air_gap), not preferred and not integrated; equal is enough
external anchors: 14 points worked by hand from the Resideo EN 1717 brochure ch. 7 (pp. 37-44)
AF admissible up to category 4, AG up to 3 (WaterRegsUK / WRAS ratings); garden sprayer category 4

provenance_note: Expected fluid category, admissible units, every exclusion reason, preferred unit, air-gap size, booster and integrated flags were computed by bench-src/ref/gen_plbbackflow.py, an independent Python implementation written from the published method (_plb/bf/METHOD.md: EN 1717 category chain, protection matrix as reproduced in the Honeywell/Resideo EN 1717 brochure, published exclusion order and preference order), not from the page code. The library of applications is read from the METHOD.md table as input data.
